answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers prove fraud. A newcomer starts at the bottom, like a willow sapling, and earns trust slowly through verified work, so an attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, since each one must pay the same bond and climb the same slow ladder. At the zenith of this design, reputation becomes a scarce asset, and saffron-priced honesty, rare, verified and hard to fake, is what the market actually rewards.
